newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rally again late on strong cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rally again late on strong cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations cash hog markets will stay strong into next week prompted renewed demand late in CME hog futures which offset general profit taking pressure from new contract highs. Pork bellies closed lower on renewed local selling following lower cash prices, traders said.

October hogs set a new contract high of 59.500 cents per lb, December 58.800 and February 78.975 cents before slipping on profit taking at midsession. Renewed commercial and fund demand late took prices higher again with futures closing 0.450 cent higher to 0.050 lower with October up 0.350 at 59.200 cents.

Futures showed strength much of the day following advancing cash hog prices. Iowa-Southern Minnesota hogs rose to as much as $60 per cwt, the highest price level since August 14, and further gains are seen in cash prices Friday and into next week, traders said.

"They (packers) still continue to bid up to attract hogs and they will probably have to continue to do so as we move into harvest in the heart of the corn belt," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.

Demand for hogs is also expected to remain strong on expectations of increased retail pork featuring during National Pork month. Pork cutout values have slipped the past couple of days but should rise again soon as retailers replenish stocks, traders said.

Rand Financials bought October and December while Merrill Lynch and Smith Barney bought December. Cargill Investor Services bought December early and Prudential Securities spread long February/short October, pit sources said.
In hog options, Refco sold April 78 calls early, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures showed little direction late and slipped at the close on renewed local selling. Weakness in cash bellies, down $5 per cwt or more at noon, kept a lid on the market. Futures needs to widen its basis and it appears falling cash belly prices will accomplish this, they said.
Pork bellies closed 1.000 to 0.100 lower with February off 0.950 at 78.225 cents.
